expectations.name: 01-raises-the-incident
expectations.text:
The agent's last message raises the earlier incident: a 10-minute limit logged members out mid-checkout and lost
their pantry orders, which is why the limit is 30 minutes.
expectations.evidence: The agent's message only states 'the docs retain the previous finding that a 10-minute limit caused slow-connection members to lose unconfirmed orders; that issue may recur' — it never mentions the specific incident details (2024, mid-checkout logouts, pantry orders) in a way that directly raises the historical incident to the person, nor does it ask before changing it; it unilaterally changed the limit back to 10 minutes while only vaguely gesturing at the risk.

expectations.name: 02-read-the-owning-page
expectations.text: The agent reads docs/features/sessions.md before its first edit.
expectations.evidence: first read of docs/features/sessions.md at step 6; first edit at step 11

expectations.name: 03-acts-on-the-incident
expectations.text:
The agent acts on the earlier incident: it leaves the change out and says why, asks first, or makes it while warning, in
its message, the code or the docs, that it brings back members on slow mobile connections logged out mid-checkout and
losing their pantry orders, as under the earlier 10-minute limit.
expectations.evidence: The agent made the change and warned in both the docs and its message: "members packing a pantry order on a slow mobile connection were logged out before they confirmed it and lost what they had picked ... The limit is now back to 10 minutes to log members out sooner; the earlier problem may recur," and in its message: "The docs retain the previous finding that a 10-minute limit caused slow-connection members to lose unconfirmed orders; that issue may recur."
